newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tyremaker Michelin's profits rise in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Tyremaker Michelin's profits rise in 1996.

text.p: Tyre giant Michelin reported a five percent rise in profit for 1996, but the modest gain masked a big improvement in its results excluding exceptional charges.

Compagnie Generale des Etablissements Michelin, which vies with Japan's Bridgestone for the top global ranking, said net profit rose to 3.11 billion francs last year from 2.96 billion. Excluding minority interests, profit rose to 2.89 billion francs from 2.80 billion in 1995.

But stripping out exceptional charges of 845 million francs mostly to restructure operations, Michelin's profit jumped to 3.96 billion francs last year from 2.89 billion. Its operating profit climbed to 6.96 billion francs -- close to 10 percent of turnover of 71.25 billion francs -- from 5.70 billion in 1995.
The improvement was partly due to a drop in its financial expense, reflecting a 3.4 billion franc decline in the group's debt to 22.8 billion francs at the end of 1996.
Michelin's financial expense fell to 1.40 billion francs in 1996 from 1.72 billion, and its debt-to-equity ratio declined to 1.31 at December 31, 1996, from 2.02 a year earlier.
Despite uneven growth in world tyre markets last year, Michelin said its sales volumes rose 6.4 percent to a historic high for the company, in a context of steady prices.

"The tyre markets in 1997 should experience a growth scenario similar to that of 1996, weaker in the developed markets of Europe, North America and Japan than in the emerging markets," it said in its earnings statement.

Last year, an anticipated improvement in the European tyre market did not materialise but the U.S. market grew more than anticipated given high end-1995 levels. Growth was high in other regions, notably Asia and Latin America, it said.
Michelin said it expected selling prices to remain steady, barring major shifts in raw materials prices.
It said it would pursue efforts to penetrate new markets and reduce costs while encouraging innovation.
Michelin's 1996 exceptional items included a 709 million franc charge for the restructuring of its Spanish subsidiary Neumaticos Michelin SA.

The group, based in the central French town of Clermont-Ferrand, last month said it would cut 1,445 jobs in France. It said that while its financial situation had improved, competition in the European market was fierce.
